identity.title: Powered Industrial Truck Pre-Shift Inspection Log – Forklift FL-2 (Toyota 8FGU25, propane), September 2026 – Portland Warehouse (photo copy)
identity.site: Portland — 4410 NW Front Ave, Portland, Oregon 97210

scan.summary: This is a photo of the September 2026 pre-shift inspection log for forklift FL-2 at the Portland warehouse. It is a record, so it is judged on whether it is complete and up to date, not against a written standard. The rows you can see cover Sep 1–17, day shift only. There are two missing weekdays, a horn defect with no repair record, and nothing visible after Sep 17. Company name, truck, month and the header all come from page 1, the only page.
scan.freshness_note: The last visible entry is Sep 17, 2026, which is 10 days before today (2026-09-27). The photo cuts off at the bottom edge, so there may be more rows. Ask for a flat scan or the original sheet covering Sep 18 to date.

gaps.title: No inspection recorded Sep 3 and Sep 4
gaps.description: There are no rows for Thursday Sep 3 or Friday Sep 4, both weekdays. The hour meter reads 4,819 on Sep 2 and 4,834 on Sep 7. That is 15 hours, against about 6–7 hours per logged day. This suggests the truck was used on about two days with no pre-shift inspection recorded.
gaps.fix: Find out whether FL-2 was used on Sep 3–4 and whether inspections were done but not written down. If it was used without being checked, retrain operators on checking before every shift. Keep a note explaining the gap with the log.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7), adopted by reference in Oregon under OAR 437-002-0220 (Oregon rule number OAR 437-002-1910.178)
gaps.locator: Page 1, between the Sep 2 and Sep 7 rows
gaps.quote: examine before each shift; do not use if a defect affects safety.

gaps.title: Horn defect Sep 9 with no repair or out-of-service record
gaps.description: The horn is marked X with the note 'Horn not working' on Sep 9. The next day it is ticked OK, with no note saying it was repaired or that the truck was taken out of service. The hour meter kept going up (4,847 to 4,853), so the truck may have been used with a safety defect.
gaps.fix: Find or create the work order or repair record for the horn fix on Sep 9–10. Keep it with the log. Add a way on the form to record the out-of-service tag and the repair sign-off whenever an X is marked.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7) and 1910.178(p)(1), adopted by reference in Oregon under OAR 437-002-0220
gaps.locator: Page 1, Sep 9 and Sep 10 rows, Horn and Notes columns

gaps.title: Entries after Sep 17 not visible
gaps.description: The photo ends at the Sep 17 row, where the sheet runs off the bottom of the image. Weekday entries for Sep 18–25 would be expected by today and cannot be seen.
gaps.fix: Supply a complete flat scan of the September sheet, or the continuation page, covering Sep 18 to date.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7), adopted by reference in Oregon under OAR 437-002-0220

scan.confidence_notes: The photo is slightly skewed but readable. I am sure of the dates, hour readings, operator initials, the X on the horn on Sep 9, and both notes. The claim that the truck was used on Sep 3–4 is my own calculation from the hour-meter jump, not something the log says. I cannot tell whether rows exist after Sep 17, because the image cuts off. I also cannot tell whether other shifts use FL-2. Oregon adopts 29 CFR 1910.178 by reference (OAR 437-002-0220) and adds its own rules in OAR 437-002-0227; I have not checked whether 0227 adds anything about inspection records. This looks like the same document as the log already on file, not a new version.
